round1.verdict: Setup is not adequate for the Main bound: it imposes no hypothesis tying f to the constant 1, so "sup_K |f| ≤ 1" is false for admissible data (K = {0}, f ≡ 2). Compactness plus continuity yields only that sup_K |f| is finite and attained; the bound needs an explicit normalization such as |f| ≤ 1 on K (equivalently ||f||_∞ ≤ 1), which Setup omits. Minor: if K = ∅ is permitted, sup_K |f| = −∞ (or is undefined), so K ≠ ∅ should be assumed or excluded; and continuity is stronger than required for finiteness — boundedness of f (or upper semicontinuity for a one-sided bound) would suffice, so continuity is an unused-strength assumption rather than an error.
gaps: Missing hypothesis: Setup never assumes |f| ≤ 1 (or any bound) on K, so the Main bound sup_K |f| ≤ 1 does not follow and is false in general (e.g. f ≡ 2); add the normalization to the Setup hypotheses.
Quantifier/edge case: if K = ∅ is allowed, sup_K |f| is −∞ or undefined, so K ≠ ∅ must be assumed or the claim restricted.
Unused strength: continuity is stronger than needed — boundedness (or upper semicontinuity for a one-sided version) suffices for the sup to be finite; compactness is what makes the sup attained.

round2.verdict: Round 2 — "Main bound": the claim does not survive as stated. sup_K |f| ≤ 1 is asserted with no hypothesis tying f to 1, and under the current Setup (K compact, f continuous) it is false: K = {0}, f ≡ 2 gives sup = 2 > 1. This is not a defect of the omitted proof — no proof exists, since compactness plus continuity give only finiteness and attainment of sup_K |f|. The missing ingredient is a hypothesis, not an argument: |f| ≤ 1 on K (equivalently ||f||_∞ ≤ 1), added to Setup. Given that hypothesis the bound is immediate (1 is an upper bound of {|f(x)| : x ∈ K}, so sup ≤ 1), so the "proof omitted" line is defensible only as a one-line triviality once the normalization is stated; as written it conceals the missing hypothesis. Compactness and K ≠ ∅ are needed only for finiteness/attainment, not for the inequality itself, and continuity remains unused strength for the bound. The sharpness remark also presupposes the normalization, since equality requires admissible f with |f| ≡ 1.
gaps: Main bound is false under the stated Setup: no hypothesis links f to the constant 1 (K = {0}, f ≡ 2 is admissible and gives sup_K |f| = 2). Add |f| ≤ 1 on K (||f||_∞ ≤ 1) to Setup; no proof can derive the claim from compactness and continuity alone.

Omitting the proof is acceptable only after that hypothesis is added, where the argument is one line (1 bounds every |f(x)|, hence bounds the sup). As written, the omission hides the missing hypothesis rather than compressing a routine argument.
Compactness (with K ≠ ∅) supplies finiteness and attainment of the sup, not the bound; continuity is stronger than needed for either the inequality or finiteness (boundedness suffices).
The Discussion's sharpness claim depends on the same normalization: equality needs admissible f with |f| ≡ 1, and the draft as it stands admits f ≡ 2, which contradicts the bound.
